lifecycles.name: Record journal coordination

states.name: No retained journal
states.meaning: journal.json is absent; this is physical absence, not a stored phase. A writer lock may still exist, and absence alone does not make a reader snapshot available or establish cleanup success.

states.name: Prepared journal
states.meaning: A validated retained journal has phase=prepared and exact before/candidate evidence. Targets may match a mixture of retained before and candidate values during an unfinished transaction; that mixture is not usable current state.

states.name: Committed journal
states.meaning: A validated retained journal has phase=committed. Every target must match its candidate identity; before-state targets are inconsistent. Only verified completion/cleanup is admissible, never restore.

transitions.trigger: Changed publication retains its recovery basis.
guards: The writer owns exclusion and the current candidate, before-set, expected revision, targets, and declared reads have passed their applicable checks.
The bounded successful-publication receipt has been prepared; unchanged and preview paths have already terminated.
effects: Write exact before/candidate snapshots, identities, write/read sets, transaction ID, and created-directory tracking as phase=prepared before any authoritative replacement.

transitions.trigger: Changed publication or explicit complete finishes the exact candidate.
guards: Ownership and known target checks remain valid, all candidate identities have been observed, and the declared read basis has been rechecked after publication.
Recovery additionally verifies the exact requested journal identity; unknown target bytes or an untrusted journal block transition.
effects: Persist phase=committed with the retained transaction evidence. Subsequent failure cannot authorize before-state restoration.

transitions.trigger: Explicit restore or a guarded precommit error path finishes restoration.
guards: Exact retained before bytes are verified and each target remains in its known before/candidate set at observed checks.
Restoration and permitted created-directory cleanup complete under owned exclusion.
effects: Remove the exact retained journal, then release the owned lock. Explicit restore returns recovered; safe automatic restoration reports the original publication failure.

transitions.trigger: Successful publication cleanup or explicit complete cleanup finishes.
guards: The exact committed candidate is verified; an explicit recovery complete also verifies current journal identity and its declared read basis.
The writer still owns exclusion; cleanup succeeds without guessing target or journal state.
effects: Remove the retained journal, then release the lock and return the already prepared saved or recovered receipt. Missing output delivery does not undo commitment.

constraints: prepared and committed are the only stored journal phases. No retained journal is a descriptive absence state; malformed, missing-when-required, stale, or unknown journal/target data is a rejection condition, not a new phase or an automatic repair transition.
A live writer lock makes the reader gate busy; a malformed/dead-owner lock or any retained journal makes it recovery-required. Even after journal removal, an unreleased lock keeps readers gated.
Without lock or retained journal, snapshot still checks gate/epoch and record revision before and after observation. Observed interference produces conflict rather than a usable mixed snapshot.

Writer and recovery exclusion update private lock/epoch coordination before authoritative effects. Preview uses the nonwriting snapshot path; unchanged execution may have private coordination effects but creates no journal.

An interruption can leave the same retained phase with partial or unknown effects. There is no inferred success/cleanup transition. Recovery validates the current evidence and observed target identities before selecting an admitted path.

This lifecycle describes storage coordination only. It does not prescribe engineering workflow stages, approvals, Scenario execution order, a new process/service, or stronger external-editor exclusion than the retained contract.
